energy expenditure, with each 1 °C rise in core temperature raising it by 13%. The impact of the cerebral injury on poststroke metab-
olism, i.e., resting energy expenditure at different levels of stroke severity, has not been fully investigated. Evidence for metabolic
injury responses based on hormonal proﬁles and changes in blood glucose concentration in the acute phase is limited. Hypergly-
cemia is common following stroke and has been associated with increased morbidity and mortality. Hyperglycemia can be attrib-
uted to overt or latent diabetes mellitus, stress responses, and effects of glucose intolerance in elderly subjects. Elevated plasma
cortisol and catecholamine concentrations representing a transient stress response have been reported in the ﬁrst 72 h following
stroke. Nitrogen requirements following stroke can be estimated using reference ranges based on body weight, or using nitrogen
balance studies.
